source.title: What Survives Distillation? A Mechanistic Interpretability Study of GPT-2 and DistilGPT-2

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Some table and figure material is flattened, but the relevant results are also described in the text.
record.tranche_reason: It applies IOI clean/corrupted activation patching and IOI performance measures to GPT-2 and a new student model, DistilGPT-2, using the original circuit-analysis approach.
record.gate_note: The paper reports IOI performance, patching, attribution, and name-mover matching results. Its TinyStories representational analyses and its separate Greater-Than circuit results do not test these claim versions and are omitted. It does not report an ablation of the main name-mover heads followed by a test for backup-head takeover.
record.test_reason: It applies IOI logit difference, head and path patching, DLA and name-mover matching to a new model, the depth-distilled DistilGPT-2. This bears on V3: whether the same head classes carry IOI in another model. It does not re-test the GPT-2 circuit (V1), backup heads (V2), methods (V4), evaluation sensitivity (V5) or prompt variants (V6). T3 (new setting) fits better than T1.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that the IOI circuit collapses completely in DistilGPT-2: the task is failed with a sign reversal, available heads give negligible recovery, and no matched head reproduces name-mover function. They attribute this to the pipeline extending beyond the student's depth, in contrast with the Greater-Than circuit, which survives through remapping. They suggest, without testing it, a repeated-name heuristic for the negative logit difference, and caution that an alternative residual IOI mechanism is not ruled out.
record.recipe_differences: Uses IOI clean/corrupted prompts, logit-difference performance measurement, and activation patching, but applies them to a depth-distilled student and restricts causal analysis to the seven IOI heads and three within-student paths available in its six layers; it does not re-test the complete GPT-2 circuit.
record.problems: The analysis covers one teacher-student pair and two circuits. IOI patching is restricted to seven available heads and three paths, and the authors do not rule out an alternative residual IOI mechanism. The prompt results are not broken down by template. Some reported IOI patching results are qualitative rather than numerical.
record.rows_left_out: No further IOI circuit results bearing on the listed versions were omitted. The paper's CKA, logit-lens, attention-summary, SAE, perplexity, and Greater-Than results were left out because they do not test these IOI claim versions.

untested.parts: The GPT-2 small 26-head circuit and its faithfulness, completeness and minimality are not re-tested. GPT-2 is used only for behaviour, DLA and attention-pattern references.
Name movers are not ablated in GPT-2, and backup-head takeover is not tested.

Only one other model (DistilGPT-2) is tested. Other sizes, model families and training checkpoints are not tested, nor is reuse of IOI components for other tasks (the GT circuit is analysed separately, not as IOI-component reuse).
No alternative circuit-discovery methods, ablation types or metrics are compared.
The study does not vary ablation, metric or prompt distribution.
There is no per-template or name-order breakdown and no prompts with more names; results are aggregated over 15 templates.

missing.what: Results for the other two of the three inter-head paths within layers 0–5; only PT→IND is reported.
Per-head numerical patching recovery for the 7 available heads (previous-token, duplicate-token, induction), which the text summarises only as negligible.
Per-class DLA values for the IOI circuit classes in DistilGPT-2, described only as approximately zero.

record.verdict_notes: The V6 links and V6 label from the reader were removed: aggregate failure across templates in a different model is not a test of prompt-variant robustness of the circuit. The V3 label is limits_scope rather than challenges, because the absence of the circuit coincides with the model not performing IOI at all. The paper states that 19 of 24 IOI heads are structurally absent in the student (Table 1 lists 26), so the analysis covers only 7 early heads. There is one teacher–student pair and code release is not stated.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not re-test the full GPT-2 small 26-head circuit or its faithfulness, completeness, and minimality criteria in GPT-2 small. Its IOI circuit interventions are on DistilGPT-2.
It does not ablate main name-mover heads and test whether backup heads take over.
Only DistilGPT-2 is tested as another model. Other model sizes, model families, checkpoints, and reuse of IOI components for other tasks are not tested.
No alternative circuit-finding methods, ablation types, or evaluation metrics are compared as competing methods for recovering the IOI circuit.
The paper does not vary ablation type or prompt distribution to measure evaluation sensitivity. It reports several IOI measures, but does not test how the evaluation changes across those choices.
IOI prompts cover 15 syntactic templates in aggregate, but results are not broken down by template or name order. Prompts with more than two names are not tested.

relationships.condition: DistilGPT-2 (6-layer depth-distilled student of GPT-2), IOI prompts from 15 templates
relationships.reason: The student fails IOI itself, below chance with a negative logit difference (r2, r4 against r1, r3). Its available early IOI heads give negligible or small patching effects and the PT→IND path is non-significant (r5–r8). DLA is near zero (r15 against r14), and no matched head preserves name-mover attention (r9–r13). So the circuit is not carried in a depth-distilled model, but the model does not do the task either; this restricts V3 rather than showing another model doing IOI by different means.
relationships.display_finding: Across 15 templates, DistilGPT-2 performs below chance with negative logit difference, negligible or small early-head patching effects, a nonsignificant previous-token-to-induction path, near-zero direct logit attribution and no matched name-mover attention.
